audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL and CL logic: EIP-4844 blob transactions and gas economics (EL), KZG point evaluation precompile (EL), transaction announcement protocol (EL P2P), fork ID peer validation (EL P2P), Capella withdrawal lifecycle and BLS credential changes (CL), Electra validator attestation and execution request processing (CL), Electra and Deneb light client sync protocols (CL), and Fulu polynomial commitment sampling (CL).

out_of_scope: General EVM execution beyond blob-specific opcodes
General beacon chain state transition beyond covered specs

threats: Provide invalid execution payloads with malformed requests

cl_vectors.entry_point: Light Client Sync Protocol (Beacon API / P2P)

misclassified_entities.reason: In spec_4d55087408ba.json (Electra Validator Deposits), 'Execution Layer' is listed as external entity. When auditing both EL and CL, the EL itself is an in-scope target component, not an external entity. The correct external entity is the interface through which EL communicates with CL (Engine API). Reclassified as EXT-EL-VIA-ENGINE-API.

In spec_5836f4ec6867.json (Fulu Poly), 'Block Producer' is a validator internal to the CL system. It is not an external entity. The data it produces (blobs) originate from external users who submitted blob transactions. Removed from external entities.

trusted_external_entities.name: User/DApp via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: JSON-RPC API (eth_sendRawTransaction for blob txs, eth_subscribe for completedTransaction, eth_newCompletedTransactionFilter)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated public API. Users can submit arbitrary blob transactions, subscription requests, and filter creation requests. All input must be fully validated including transaction format, KZG commitments, versioned hash prefixes, and blob counts.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via devp2p (eth/65+)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: devp2p eth protocol (NewPooledTransactionHashes, GetPooledTransactions, PooledTransactions, blob sidecar gossip, fork ID in ENR/handshake)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P network. Peers can send fake transaction hash announcements, return wrong transactions for requested hashes, gossip invalid blob sidecars, or lie about their fork ID. All data requires full validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Discovery Network Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated discovery protocol. Peers advertise fork IDs in ENRs without cryptographic proof of correctness. Fork ID can be spoofed to bypass pre-filtering.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Engine API (GetPayloadResponse with execution_requests, execution payload with withdrawals)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT between co-located CL and EL clients. However, the EL could be buggy or compromised, so the CL must validate execution request ordering, format, per-payload limits, withdrawal root consistency, and all payload fields (parent_hash, prev_randao, timestamp).

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator Operator via Beacon API/P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: SignedBLSToExecutionChange message (Beacon API or P2P gossip)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any entity can submit BLS-to-execution credential change messages. The CL must verify: validator exists, current credentials use BLS prefix, pubkey hash matches, and BLS signature is valid using fork-agnostic domain. This is a security-critical irreversible operation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Light Client Sync Source via P2P/Beacon API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Light Client Sync Protocol (LightClientUpdate, LightClientBootstrap messages)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Light client servers provide updates containing Merkle proofs and sync committee signatures. Data is unauthenticated and must be verified via fork-aware generalized indices, Merkle branch validation, and sync committee signature verification.

trusted_external_entities.name: Data Column Provider via P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P gossip (DataColumnSidecar containing cells and KZG proofs)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Nodes providing data column sidecars for data availability sampling. Cells and proofs must be batch-verified via Fiat-Shamir challenge aggregation and BLS12-381 pairing checks. Invalid proofs must be detected and rejected.

trusted_external_entities.name: Smart Contract via EVM CALL
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Precompile call to address 0x0A (point evaluation precompile)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any smart contract can call the point evaluation precompile with arbitrary 192-byte input. The precompile must validate input length, versioned hash format, KZG commitment and proof validity, and field element ranges.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full blob transaction validation required: type-3 format, non-nil 'to' address, secp256k1 signature, min 1 blob, versioned hash prefix 0x01, sender balance coverage for execution + blob gas, max_fee_per_blob_gas >= blob base fee. For subscriptions: filter parameter validation (from/to address format, hasReturnData boolean).
Validate devp2p packet size (10MB limit), hash count limits (4096 for announcements, 256 for requests), transaction content matches announced hashes, blob sidecar KZG proof verification.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: ENR fork ID field and eth handshake fork ID exchange
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Fork ID is not cryptographically authenticated. Validation uses CRC32 comparison and subset/superset relationship checks. Malicious peers can lie about fork ID; this is a best-effort filter, not a security boundary.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Engine API GetPayloadResponse (execution_requests: deposits, withdrawals, consolidations)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: JWT-authenticated channel, but CL must validate: execution request type ordering (ascending, no duplicates), per-payload request limits, deserialization correctness. Withdrawal root in payload must match hash_tree_root of expected withdrawals from get_expected_withdrawals. Parent hash, prev_randao, and timestamp consistency required.

Must verify: validator index exists, current withdrawal credentials use 0x00 BLS prefix, BLS pubkey hash matches credential bytes 1-31, BLS signature is valid using fork-agnostic DOMAIN_BLS_TO_EXECUTION_CHANGE. This is an irreversible one-way credential migration.

Must resolve fork-appropriate generalized indices (Altair vs Electra) based on attested slot epoch. Verify finalized root Merkle branch and sync committee Merkle branch using resolved gindices. Validate sync committee BLS aggregate signature. Fork-specific execution payload header hashing (Capella/Deneb/Electra) for backward compatibility.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P DataColumnSidecar gossip (cells and KZG proofs)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Batch verify cell KZG proofs using Fiat-Shamir challenge derivation and BLS12-381 pairing check. Deduplicate commitments for efficiency. If batch verification fails, must perform individual cell verification to identify invalid proofs. Recovery requires at least 50% valid cells; corrupted cells must be excluded before recovery attempt.

Validate input exactly 192 bytes. Parse and validate versioned hash (0x01 prefix), z and y as BLS12-381 field elements (< BLS_MODULUS), 48-byte G1 commitments and proofs. Verify computed versioned hash matches input. Verify KZG proof via pairing check. Fixed 50,000 gas cost. All cryptographic exceptions caught and converted to KZGProofError.
